## Summary

CIG ShangHai Co., Ltd. is a China-based maker of information and communications equipment, listed in Shanghai under ticker 603083, whose products include optical fibre and copper access gear, home wireless interconnection products, Ethernet switches, IoT gateways and high-speed optical modules, sold mainly to overseas markets [2]. Its own site gives the group name Cambridge Industries Group, a founding year of 2005, a 2014 relocation of its headquarters and R&D centre to a new facility and of its manufacturing to the Pudong area of Shanghai, the Shanghai listing in November 2017 and a Hong Kong listing in October 2025 [1]. The IEEE registry lists 25 MA-L blocks to "CIG SHANGHAI CO LTD" at a Chenhang Road address in Shanghai, while 12 more MA-L blocks are registered to "Cambridge Industries(Group) Co.,Ltd." and one to "Cambridge Industries Group (CIG)", spellings this entry does not cover [3].

CIG describes itself as a supplier of PON ONTs, home and enterprise Wi-Fi equipment, routers, gateways and LTE/5G small cells alongside optical transceivers [4]. Much of that ships under operators' or other vendors' brands: WikiDevi records the Nokia XS-010X-Q XGS-PON ONU as CIG's XG-99YF, built on a Cortina Systems CA8271A [5], and the Google Fiber Jack GFLT210 SFP module as CIG-made on a Realtek RTL9601CI [6]. A MAC in a CIG block is therefore most likely a fibre ONT, gateway or Wi-Fi CPE handed out by an ISP rather than a personal device [4][5]. No FCC grantee code is listed because the FCC ID databases refused requests from the session that wrote this entry, and nothing is filled in from memory; no security advisories are listed, and randomization is unknown.
